added: A dances spreadsheet you exported now comes back in with its composed and interpreted dates, interpreters, mixed level, star rating and Barnes reference in their own fields, and a square's kind, repeat order, new partner and singing call and the published sources in the calling notes, under their column names.

When you map a spreadsheet's columns, Calling notes, with the label is now offered for any spreadsheet, not only a text file, and a column named like one of the app's own fields, such as Rating or Composed, starts on that field rather than on a custom field of the same name.
fixed: A dances spreadsheet you exported comes back in with each formation's detail, and with each figure's note on its figure instead of as an extra figure.

A spreadsheet dance whose formation the app can't read now starts on the first formation its type offers, such as Duple minor for an English dance or Square for a square, instead of a contra's Improper.
A spreadsheet or text file with a very long run of brackets in its figures no longer freezes the import.
A title that starts with an apostrophe before =, +, - or @ keeps its apostrophe when you export it to a spreadsheet and import it again.
A new choice field made from a spreadsheet column no longer gets two options that differ only in case.
The first time a spreadsheet import creates a custom field, the app now shows the same notice it shows when you create your first custom field yourself.

added: CsvColumnTarget gains composed, interpreters, interpreted, mixedLevel, rating and barnesReference; the CSV import reads them into the draft (interpreters into StructuredDraft.interpreterNames).
fixed: The CSV import reads a formation's detail after ' — ', defaults a missing formation to its form's first offered shape, folds an indented line under a figure into that figure's note, keeps a figure line longer than maxFreeTextEntryLength as text unparsed, and folds new choice options by case.
The Caller's Box figure dialect blanks (…) and […] annotations in time linear in the line.
guardCsvFormula doubles a value's own leading apostrophe before a formula character, so unguardCsvFormula gives the value back.
